dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: #What are you up to, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: For once, I have the day off. I'm gonna make the most of it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: It's pretty nice. Thanks for the invite.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I just did a few laps of the place. The general layout's really quite interesting. Did you study landscape design?

choices.text: No, I just went with my gut.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Ah, so you're one of those naturally gifted types. A self-taught prodigy.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: This has piqued my interest, though... I wonder if I should study for a qualification in landscape design?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why not? Go for it!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Wow, I like the enthusiasm, haha. Thanks for the support.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I guess I'll give it a shot, then. But could you possibly let me borrow this site before the exam, for me to practice on?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: In return, let's see... I'll cover all your roasted Lavender Melon costs leading up to the exam. What do you think?

choices.text: I know a thing or two. You've studied it, too?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Actually, no, I haven't...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you want to chat?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Sure, I'm not exactly busy right now. If you've got any questions, ask away!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it that you don't like about shrine maidens?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I think you may have misunderstood me...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I have nothing against any shrine maiden. It's not even that I detest the profession. Believe me, I know every job comes with its challenges...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: The simple fact is that being a shrine maiden is just not for me. The reasons are complicated... let me think how to explain it...

choices.text: Is it to do with your family?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Hmm... You're gonna think this sounds childish, but yes, you're right. Sometimes, I just can't stand my family...

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I know they only wanted the best for me, but trying to achieve that by planning out every aspect of my life for me just made everything unbearable.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: They always treated me like I was a child, felt like they had to constantly nag me to make sure I didn't slip up. Every time I received a letter of complaint saying that I wasn't warm and friendly enough, they would be on my case about it for days.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I just don't like to smile, that's all. Doesn't mean I have any animosity towards anyone.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's understandable.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: In a nutshell, I prefer to work jobs where the metrics are clear and where I can see the actual results of my efforts.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Jobs like that come naturally to me, and they give me a chance to show my family that my choices aren't worse than theirs just because they're different.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: But the most important thing is that I no longer have to force myself to do something I don't want to do. I can live a pretty free life.

choices.text: Is it to do with you?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Yeah, I guess it must be.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Look, a lot of people just want a fortune slip hoping to get a bit of good luck, and they don't really care what's written on the slip.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: But then there are those who, for all sorts of reasons, end up in dire straits and turn to prayer as their last resort...

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: They desperately want some divine power to make all of their problems go away.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: It doesn't sit right with me. I can't bring myself to say "things'll get better" to people like that. It's just a cop-out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Actually, there's something I'd like your help with, and it has to be you.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I'm working on a "Migrant Housing Scheme"...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I know the different policies for migrant workers purchasing real estate in the different nations. But I don't know much about the local cultures...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: What kind of things do people living in different areas need be aware of? What are the local gangs, who are the local powerplayers?

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: You've been to a lot of places. Could you give me some pointers?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: What!? No! This has nothing to do with the Arataki Gang.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I'm just helping a client with their "Migration Prospectus," and I'm gonna take the opportunity to go traveling for a few days.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I'm working on something else for the other guys... the "Arataki Gang's Comprehensive Guide to Surviving and Thriving." It's progressing nicely...

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: You know what those numbskulls are like. They aren't mean-spirited, but they do cause no end of trouble.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: I can't be around them all the time. In the long term, something's gotta change.

choices.text: You're not going to leave the gang, are you?

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Of course not, at least not for now. As the de-facto manager, I still can't say I've turned the gang into something I'm proud of, and I am not gonna quit halfway.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Who knows what the future holds, though.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: If it really gets to the point where we end up parting ways, well, sometimes that's just how life goes...

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Everyone who's trying to make their life work deserves to be happy, regardless of what direction they've chosen.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Same goes for the Arataki Gang and I as for you and me. No matter where the future takes us, whether we stay together or part ways, we'll always have each other's support, won't we?

choices.text: I'll support you whatever you do!

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: If you say so, I'll hold you to it. Oral agreements are just as binding as written agreements, you know.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: So... if I do end up leaving the Arataki Gang and come looking to you for protection, you can't say no, okay? Uh... Tubby can be my witness.

response.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
response.text: Hehe, but for better or worse, it's probably not gonna happen. I don't like to rely on anyone, it doesn't suit my personality.

choices.text: Are you planning the Arataki Gang's escape?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Shinobu!

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: #Morning, {NICKNAME}. Any plans for the day? Gimme a shout if you need any help.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: When you're a freelancer like me, you get to be pretty flexible with your schedule. I can always make time where necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Shinobu.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: #Alright, {NICKNAME}, go get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I took an editing job recently, and I'm working on a manuscript right now. It's interesting, but it's gonna keep me busy for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: ...Don't be like me. Having a consistent routine is vital, so go get to bed.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Wow, there are more books here than I expected, and a wide range of genres, too...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Hmm? Wow, you even have reference books. Just from flipping through, they look pretty interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: You know... I feel right at home here. Actually, I think I might settle in for the long haul, if it's alright with you.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: I took a part-time job selling toys once. Barely managed to sell anything, and I got tons of complaints from the parents...

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Allegedly, my face mask and generally mean-looking demeanor was frightening the kids... It's funny, because I distinctly remember hearing the kids say how cool I looked as they walked by.

dialogues.speaker: Kuki Shinobu
dialogues.text: Whatever. It's in the past now, anyway.
